messages:
Alex M: Heads-up — after rolling async-batch heuristics (PR #4521) I’m seeing a clear p95 regression on the paged-flash attention path for short sequences (seq_len=32). Before: ~120ms, after: ~310ms on our dev instances. Noticed this on both dedicated and local repros.

Tara L: Ugh. Can you drop the exact config you ran and the model/size?

Alex M: repro steps: run bench_attention --model=redwood/qlora-small --seq=32 --batch=1 --kernels=paged,flash_paged_v2 --kv=enabled --warm=30 --iter=200
Output snippet:
```
p50: 45.3ms
p90: 88.1ms
p95: 310.4ms  <-- regressed
p99: 490.2ms
mean: 132.7ms
```
Before patch (same infra): p95 118.9ms.

Ben R: Did you capture a profiler trace? My hunch: the async-batch heuristic changed the work distribution so flash_paged_v2 is getting invoked with suboptimal launch params, causing serial memcpy or small-grid kernel overhead.

perf-bot: Attached profile (flame) from Alex's run: flame://perf/2087654321/trace. Key hotspot: cudaMemcpyAsync(Host->Device) ~60ms per iter and small kernel launches with grid size=1. Kernel chosen: flash_paged_v2_kernel_small_tile.

Jia W: I ran a quick bisect on main -> HEAD. Bisect points to commit de4705f (tuning: async-batch: prefer per-request batching for short seqs). That commit tweaks the batcher cutoff from 64->16 and enabled per-request coalesce. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/de4705f

Tara L: So the heuristic made more frequent kernel switches for short requests? That matches the profile. Is KV cache access pattern also changed?

Alex M: Yes — with per-request coalesce we see more KV cache lookups that miss the device cache, triggering host-device copies. When batch size=1 and seq=32 we lose amortization.

Ben R: Reproduced locally. When I force the kernel selector to pick flash_fused_v1 (old path) latency goes down to ~125ms. Quick diff of selected kernels shows extra memcpy and an extra sync inserted by the new path.

perf-bot: CI synthetic perf tests: gutter/regressions.attn.small_seq shows +160% p95 for commit de4705f on cuda-rt-12 (gpu: a100). The regression is only visible for batch<=2 and seq<=48. No regression for long seqs or batch>=8.

sre-oncall: If this is hitting production SLAs we should consider rolling back the rollout on dedicated today. Can you confirm % of requests that hit the short-seq path?

Alex M: On hosted telemetry ~14% of requests are short-seq (<=32) for some customers, and they show a 2x tail latency bump post-rollout. Will open a rollback if patch doesn't have quick fix.

Jia W: Possible fixes: 1) revert the cutoff change (64->16) 2) add a micro-batch coalescer that forces small requests into a single device-side batched kernel 3) tweak kernel selector to avoid flash_paged_v2 for batch<=2.

Ben R: I prototyped option (3) quickly: if batch_size <=2 and seq <=48 prefer fused path. Patch reduced p95 from 310 -> 128 in my repro. Simple guard in selector.

Tara L: Nice. We should also add a unit perf test for short-seq/batch=1 to CI so this doesn't slip.

Alex M: Agree. I'll open a hotfix PR that pins selector for short-seq and add the CI test. If it passes we'll roll forward the fix. If not, revert commit de4705f.

perf-bot: New issue created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/789 — "paged-flash: p95 regression for short sequences after async-batch heuristic change". Attached CI perf run comparisons.

sre-oncall: FYI I prepped rollback patch on prod routing; hold until Alex confirms hotfix results.

Ben R: Follow-up note — also check KV prefetch path. When coalescing changed we started prefetching independent prefixes per-request which increases host->device churn. Short-term selector guard buys us time to properly change the KV caching prefetch strategy.

Alex M: Action items: 1) open hotfix PR (selector guard) — Alex (in progress) 2) add short-seq perf test to CI — Alex/Tara 3) check KV prefetch behavior and propose prefetch window change — Ben/Jia 4) decide rollback if hotfix fails — SRE.

Tara L: Thx. Ping here when PR is up and CI perf comparison is attached. :thumbsup:

Alex M: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4623 — contains selector guard + perf test. Running CI perf now.

perf-bot: CI perfsummary: before(de4705f) p95=118.9ms, after(de4705f) p95=310.4ms, hotfix(PR/4623) p95=129.6ms — perf test passed.

sre-oncall: Good — hold rollback. Ship hotfix and monitor prod traces for next 24h.

Ben R: I'll follow up with a deeper kernel launch config audit next sprint to avoid similar regressions.

Alex M: Closing loop: pushing rollout for hotfix to 10% canary now. Will report back after 4h.

Tara L: Awesome, thanks everyone.
